title: Commissioners appointed to SA Royal Commission into AI
key_facts: The South Australian Government has appointed three Commissioners to its Royal Commission into Artificial Intelligence and released the inquiry's Terms of Reference.

Dr Iain Ross AO, an economist and former Federal Court judge, leads the Commission; he was officially appointed Chair on Thursday 1 Oct 2026, alongside Commissioners Kate Pounder and Professor Christopher Manning.
Kate Pounder was the inaugural CEO of the Tech Council of Australia and has worked with OpenAI; Professor Christopher Manning is described as the lead AI researcher at Stanford University.

The Government says the inquiry will be broad and evidence-based, covering the economic and societal opportunities and implications of AI for South Australia, including how the state can use AI safely and responsibly for the public good.
It will examine AI across education, employment, economic opportunity, regulation, community life and public services.
Engagement will include public submissions, community forums, surveys, industry roundtables and targeted consultations.
The Commission is expected to hand its final report to government in mid 2027.
